name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: IRGC drones at Bahrain 13 Nov; Sirik hit 12 Nov
summary: IRGC says it hit a US radar in Bahrain after a strike on Sirik; CENTCOM says it downed two IRGC drones on 13 Nov
state: Iranian state media said the port town of Sirik in Hormozgan was hit by enemy fire on 12 Nov; the IRGC said it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response, its first claimed attack on US assets in a Gulf state since early September (Al Jazeera, 13 Nov). CENTCOM said it shot down two IRGC one-way attack drones on 13 Nov with no injuries or damage, and that it continues to enforce a naval blockade of Iranian ports. President Trump said he would not hesitate to renew strikes (Times of Israel, 13 Nov). Active state-on-state strikes and attacks on Gulf shipping set the Alert.
for_you: British nationals in Bahrain, the UAE, Qatar, Oman and Iran should follow FCDO travel advice, which can change at short notice. Airspace closures and flight disruption tend to follow strikes in the region.
rubric_hit: Alert: active strikes between states (Sirik strike 12 Nov; IRGC drones at US assets in Bahrain 13 Nov)

sources.title: Al Jazeera — US denies Iran's claim it hit radar sites in Bahrain

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
